transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Um... I guess I came in because I’ve started doing things lately that actually kind of scare me. Like, I'll just walk out in the middle of big system deployments at work, which I would normally never do. Or I'll end up just driving around late at night with no real plan or destination. I just... that is definitely not how I’ve ever handled stress before, so I figured I needed to talk to someone about it.
Have you been sleeping less than usual lately?

Yeah, definitely. Most nights I just... I lie there replaying pieces of this incident that happened at the office. And then when I finally do manage to fall asleep, I end up waking up really tense, either from dreams or just from some small noise in the house. I'm basically exhausted before work even starts.
How long ago did the incident at the office happen?
It happened a little over a year ago. We had this late-night cutover incident... so, yeah, it's been about 13 months now.
When you sleep very little, do you feel unusually energized rather than tired the next day?
No, definitely not. Um, I don't feel energized at all. Like I was saying, I'm just completely exhausted the next day. I basically just drag myself through work.
When you drive around or leave work unexpectedly, do you later have trouble remembering what happened during that time?

No, I don't really have that issue. I don't leave work unexpectedly or just drive around aimlessly. And my memory of the day is fine... I always remember what happened. I'm just really tired while I'm doing it.
During the office incident, were you exposed to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence?

No, nothing like that. It wasn't... I mean, no one was hurt or threatened or anything. It was just a really massive system failure that took down our whole network, and the stress of trying to fix it all night while everything was crashing around us. But no, no actual danger to anyone's life or safety.
Is the stressful situation related to that office incident still ongoing in your life?
No, it's not. The system was fixed that week, and things have been running normally since then. So the actual situation is over.
When did these symptoms first begin in relation to the office incident?
Well, they started pretty much right after that late-night cutover incident. So it's been going on for a little over a year now... I'd say about 13 months.
Are these symptoms mainly triggered by reminders of the office incident?

No, not really. I mean, it's not like walking into a server room or looking at a network dashboard sets things off for me. I haven't noticed any specific reminders of that night triggering them... they just kind of happen on their own, regardless of what I'm doing.
Over the past six months, have you been worrying excessively about several different areas of your life, such as work, finances, health, or family?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have normal worries, I guess, like anyone else, but I haven't been obsessing or excessively worrying about my finances or health or anything like that. It's not a constant worry about different parts of my life.
Since the office incident, have you felt persistently sad or hopeless?
No, I haven't really felt that way. I mean, I have my rough days, sure, but I wouldn't say I feel persistently sad or hopeless about things. It's not like a depression.
How much have these symptoms interfered with your work, relationships, or everyday life?

Well, it's definitely having an impact. At work, I just had my performance review, and it was the first time I've ever been told I'm missing key handoffs. My manager said I've been leaving meetings abruptly and that the rest of the team is basically having to work around me. And then at home... my husband told me recently that it feels like I'm barely even present anymore. So, yeah, it's interfering a lot.
Since the office incident, have you felt persistently anxious or emotionally distressed?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, even on quiet days, I just feel this mix of fear and shame sitting right in my chest. I keep feeling like I should have handled everything better than I did. And there's just this constant sense that something could still happen if I let my guard down for a second.
Do unwanted memories of the office incident repeatedly come into your mind when you do not intend to think about it?

Yes, they do. It happens out of nowhere, really. Like, especially if I have to go near that conference area at work, or even if someone just raises their voice on a call... I'll just get hit with these images and sounds from that night. It comes on so strongly that I'll completely lose track of what I was saying right in the middle of a sentence.
Have you been deliberately avoiding thoughts, conversations, places, or activities that remind you of the office incident?

Yes, I definitely do. I actually take the long way around the building now just to avoid going near that floor whenever I can. And if people at work start talking about the contractor or the cutover, I just... I shut the conversation down immediately or walk away. I just don't want to think about it.
Since the office incident, have you felt emotionally detached or cut off from other people?
No, not really. I mean, I still talk to my friends and my family the same amount. I don't feel disconnected from them or anything like that.

inference.note: Intrusive memories, avoidance, hyperarousal, distress, and impairment support an other specified trauma- and stressor-related disorder; however, the office incident did not involve death, serious injury, or sexual violence, ruling out PTSD. The persistence and symptom pattern make F43.89 more likely than unspecified F43.9.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Persistent, clinically impairing stress-related symptoms began immediately after a major occupational stressor and include intrusive recollections, avoidance, hyperarousal, fear, shame, sleep disruption, and maladaptive behavioral changes. PTSD is not met because the event did not involve actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence. The prolonged course after the stressor ended and the trauma-like presentation are most consistent with other specified trauma- and stressor-related disorder/other reaction to severe stress.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent unwanted memories, images, and sounds of the office incident
Intrusive recollections are triggered by the conference area and raised voices
Intrusions are intense enough to cause loss of track of speech mid-sentence
Recurrent distressing dreams or nocturnal replay of the incident
Takes a longer route at work to avoid the floor associated with the incident
Avoids conversations about the contractor or cutover
Attempts to suppress or shut down thoughts and discussions about the incident
Persistent fear and shame related to the incident
Persistent self-blame that the event should have been handled better
Ongoing sense that something could happen if vigilance is relaxed
Difficulty falling asleep due to replaying the incident
Frequent awakening in a tense state in response to dreams or small noises
Marked exhaustion during the day due to poor sleep
Abruptly leaves meetings or work activities
Drives around late at night without a clear destination
Walks out during major system deployments

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms began immediately after the office incident and have persisted for approximately 13 months.
additional_requirements: Symptoms began in close temporal relationship to an identifiable occupational stressor
The stressor itself involved a major system failure but no actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence
The stressful situation ended shortly after the incident
Symptoms cause significant occupational and relationship impairment
Sleep reduction produces exhaustion rather than increased energy, arguing against a manic episode
No persistent depressed mood or hopelessness reported
No excessive generalized worry across multiple life domains reported
No amnesia for the behavioral episodes reported
